messages:
alyssa: quick follow-up from the RFC—i prototyped merging sparsity metadata into the quant profile proto and added a 'quality_slices' list. goal is a single artifact for runtime to decide precision+sparsity+slice in one handshake. thoughts?

marco: curious about on-disk size impact. we already have big profiles for some 70B models. did you measure?

alyssa: yes, did a rough diff. protobuf + sparsemask + 3 slices ~ +6KB per profile (avg). main cost is storing per-slice calibration vectors. overall repo +100MB if we keep all historical profiles, but runtime only fetches active profile.

sasha: +6KB seems fine if runtime caching avoids repeated downloads. bigger risk is compatibility: what happens when runtime sees unknown slice keys?

alyssa: plan is graceful: runtime checks profile.version and slice_hash. unknown slices -> fallback to canonical slice (index 0) and emit telemetry: `quant.profile.slice_unrecognized`. ops policy will decide whether to reject or allow with flag.

jordan: how do we represent slice matching at request time? user-supplied hint vs automatic classifier? we need deterministic matching for canary reproducibility.

alyssa: design: endpoint accepts optional `quality_slice` header or a `slice_selector` object. if absent, runtime runs a quick lightweight selector: token_length + prompt_embedding_norm + request_type -> hash -> slice. selector is deterministic given same model+profile.

marco: selector latency? can't add >200us to hot path.

alyssa: bench: simple 128-dot prod of summary embedding and table lookup ~ 40-60us on CPU. can be optionally offloaded to worker thread; also cached per-session via KV.

sasha: what about evaluation surface? we need per-slice eval buckets and drift tracking. otherwise regressions hide in aggregated metrics.

alyssa: agreed. `quality_slices` entries include: name, sample_selector_desc, calibration_vectors, min_tokens_for_stats. we will tag eval traces with slice_name so dashboards show per-slice nps/loss and degscore.

jordan: fallback policy thresholds? example: if post-quant deg_score > 0.12 on slice, prefer higher-bit fallback automatically?

alyssa: proposing an ops-level policy object in profile: `fallback_rules`: list of `{slice, metric, threshold, fallback_profile}`. default rule: deg_score >= 0.12 -> fallback to int8_profile or cpu-safe fp16. runtime evaluates after warmup tokens (e.g., first 50 tokens) and can mid-stream switch if KV can be transferred.

marco: mid-stream switching seems hairy. KV transfer between quant variants is non-trivial. are we comfortable only doing pre-generation decisions?

alyssa: good point. MVP: pre-decide at request start. mid-stream will be experimental flag. ops will need to opt-in per-customer.

ops-bot: note: created ticket INF-2483 for telemetry events and INF-2484 for dashboard slicing.

sasha: one more: storage/consistency for per-head sparsity masks. if masks change, outputs differ a lot. recommend we include `mask_commit` and `mask_signature` in profile metadata to force invalidation when models re-sparsify.

alyssa: added to proto: `sparsity.commit` and `sparsity.signature`. runtime will reject profile if commit mismatch with model binary unless override flag set.

marco: sounds reasonable. action items?

alyssa: action items: 1) eng-ml to finalize proto PR with quality_slices + fallback_rules (alyssa) 2) eng-runtime to add slice selector + telemetry hooks (marco) 3) observability to add per-slice panels and `quant.profile.slice_unrecognized` alert (sasha) 4) ops to review INF tickets and flag experimental mid-stream fallback customers (jordan). aiming for canary next week.

jordan: i'll coordinate with customer success. schedule canary for 10% traffic of internal staging first.

marco: will start prototype in runtime branch `slice-handshake-v1`. will ping when ready for review.

alyssa: awesome. if no objections i'll open the proto PR today and tag reviewers. :thumbsup:
